name: Collins 2014 C5: 40 Hz chirp both sides, then hippocampal right (Shiva God Helmet, 40 min)
origin: Todd Murphy, 'God Helmet Sessions for the Shiva Neural System' v1H; tested in Persinger's lab, Laurentian University (Collins 2014, MA thesis, ch. 4)
summary: Condition 5 of Collins's 2014 Persinger-lab test of Todd Murphy's Shiva God Helmet software: the '40 Hz Modulated Chirp' over both sides for 20 min, then the 'Hippocampal' (LTP) field over the right side for 20 min, on the thesis's four coils per side with one left-right pair on at a time. The lab reported no specific EEG or experience effect for this condition.
notes: Condition 5 of the 8 primer-target sessions of Murphy's 'God Helmet Sessions for the Shiva Neural System' v1H that Collins (MA thesis, Laurentian University, Persinger's lab) gave to 24 students, 3 per session, 20 + 20 min (Table 3). Thesis geometry: four solenoids per side on a Velcro square, 5 cm apart vertically and 8 cm horizontally, one left-right pair on at a time, the left side stepping clockwise and the right side counter-clockwise. Its photo numbers one side's coils top, back, bottom, front, which is counter-clockwise seen from the right and, mirrored, clockwise seen from the left, as here; C5, TP7, T9h, FFT7 and their right mirrors (about 5.8 x 7.7 cm) are an inference. The Shiva files are proprietary, so the fields are stand-ins: 'Hippocampal' = a primed burst after Rose et al. 1988 (cited by Collins), as Corradini 2014 describes the Shiva file (a primer, then 4 pulses 150 ms later, 1-ms points, positive only); 1-ms pulses 10 ms apart, five trains in 1 s and 4 s of silence are assumptions; '40 Hz Modulated Chirp' (Table 3: '40 Hz Chirp') = a 40 Hz sine phase-modulated five times a second (Sculthorpe & Persinger 2003; the 3-rad depth is a guess) held 100, 120, 140 and 160 ms on successive coils, after Murphy's 'longer and longer gaps between sections of the signal as they travel around your head' (his chirp page instead shows a falling-frequency chirp). The thesis gives no step time: the hippocampal field every 200 ms, so each primer and its 4 pulses fall on the same coil (at 100 ms they would always land on different coils). The thesis measured 1-2 uT at the centre of the cap; 1.5 uT here is the peak 20 mm in front of each coil, so the field inside the head is weaker than in the thesis. Collins says each left-right pair is arranged so 'a field is generated between them' but gives no polarity, so both sides use the same drive sign. The vendor rebuild murphy-gh-chirpbi-hippr-40min uses an FT7/C5/TP7/T9 cross, 125-ms steps, 1 uT, theta-burst (Larson & Lynch) LTP and a 40-to-6 Hz sweep for the chirp. Collins reported no rise in right-frontal high-beta power for this condition; that rise, peaking at 35 min, appeared only in the two conditions with a bilateral target (4 and 8; eta2 = .19, larger in women). The EEG change was not linked to reported experiences, no clear pattern of experiences emerged, and the thesis had set an eta2 of about 30 % as its bar for a clinically conspicuous effect. Three people per condition, no sham group in this study, one lab, no replication; independent double-blind tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005; Gendle & McGrath 2012). Not for people with epilepsy or a seizure history; stop on fear, anger, headache or distress.
setting: Seated in a comfortable chair, eyes closed, in a quiet, dark room (the thesis used a shielded acoustic chamber), told that a field may or may not be on. The thesis recorded 19-channel EEG every 5 min and gave the Personal Philosophy Inventory before and a 20-item exit questionnaire after.
schedule: One 40-min session per person in the thesis. For a self-test, run it against sham with the app's Blind option and fix the measure in advance (the thesis effect: right-frontal high-beta at 35 min).
source: Collins 2014 (title page dated 2013), Quantitative differences in participants exposed to patterned, weak-intensity electromagnetic fields: investigating the Shiva, MA thesis (Psychology), Laurentian University, ch. 4 and Table 3 (the 289-point amygdaloid file of the 64-coil study in ch. 2) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/16d96136-680c-4afe-8044-f9137bd01afc ; Collins 2014, full text https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/server/api/core/bitstreams/c03e0259-4b31-410f-9552-d90c9c2b81a4/content ; Murphy, God Helmet session list https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/god-helmet/koren_session_list.htm ; Murphy, Shiva: sessions used in lab experiments (the chirp's 'longer and longer gaps') https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/shiva/shiva_demo/experiment_signals.htm ; Murphy, Shiva demo: modulated 40 Hz chirp https://www.god-helmet.com/wp/shiva/shiva_demo/mod40_chirp.htm ; Corradini 2014, MA thesis, Laurentian University (Shiva hippocampal file: primer pulse, then 4 pulses 150 ms later, 1-ms points) https://laurentian.scholaris.ca/items/1455e1f3-2f1d-47b5-93cd-23713d69e651 ; Rose, Diamond, Pang & Dunwiddie 1988, primed burst potentiation (cited by Collins for the hippocampal field) ; Sculthorpe & Persinger 2003, Percept Mot Skills 97:1031 (40 Hz phase-modulated five times per second) https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15002842/ ; Granqvist et al. 2005, Neurosci Lett 379:1 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15849873/ ; Gendle & McGrath 2012, Percept Mot Skills 114:217 https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22582690/
